questions.stem: The metal that produces a bright crimson red color in the flame test is:
questions.solution: Lithium ($\mathrm{Li}$) imparts a crimson red color to the flame. Sodium gives golden yellow, Potassium gives pale violet/lilac, and Rubidium gives reddish violet.

questions.stem: The metal that produces a bright crimson red colour in the flame test is:
questions.solution: In the flame test, Lithium imparts a crimson red (or bright crimson) colour to the flame, Sodium gives golden yellow, Potassium gives violet/lilac, and Cesium gives blue.

questions.stem: The number of alkali metal(s) among Li, Na, K, Rb, and Cs that form(s) stable superoxide(s) when reacted with excess oxygen is/are _______.
questions.solution:
Li forms primarily oxide ($\text{Li}_2\text{O}$).
Na forms peroxide ($\text{Na}_2\text{O}_2$).
K, Rb, and Cs form stable superoxides ($\text{KO}_2$, $\text{RbO}_2$, $\text{CsO}_2$) because of the large cation stabilizing the large superoxide anion.
Therefore, the number of such metals is 3.
